--- title: "Did Authors Respond to Unjournal Evaluations?" author: "The Unjournal" date: last-modified format: html: toc: true toc-depth: 3 code-fold: true code-summary: "Show code" execute: echo: true warning: false message: false freeze: auto --- ::: {.callout-note} Manual coding of 57 tracked evaluations, last updated April 2026. Methodology: two data sources combined — (a) manual assessment of author responses and paper revisions by Unjournal staff, and (b) automated PDF-comparison via the [`paper_change_analysis` tool](https://daaronr.github.io/unjournal_tools_interfaces/paper_change_analysis/) which detects line-level changes between pre- and post-evaluation PDF versions. ::: ## Overview The Unjournal commissions open, structured evaluations of working papers in economics and social science. A natural question is whether this process actually changes research: do authors engage with the feedback and revise their work? This page tabulates evidence from approximately 57 tracked evaluations based on manual assessment. For each paper where sufficient time has passed, Unjournal staff assessed whether the authors (a) formally or informally responded to the evaluation, and (b) produced an updated version of the paper that reflects the feedback. For a subset of papers, automated PDF change detection (line-level diffing of before/after versions) supplements the manual coding. The broader background and framing is discussed in [The Unjournal's knowledge base](https://globalimpact.gitbook.io/the-unjournal-project-and-communication-space/benefits-and-features/more-reliable-and-useful-evaluation/author-engagement-evidence). ## Summary ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-summary="Load data and define helpers"} library(dplyr) library(ggplot2) library(readr) library(DT) library(tidyr) library(stringr) df <- read_csv("data/author_adjustment_manual.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) # Rename columns for easier use df <- df |> rename( paper_title = label_paper_title, pubpub_link = dup_pubpub_final_links, adj_status = `Adjusted_paper?`, pub_statement = `Author's public statement about evaluation/UJ`, updated_manual = `Updated since UJ report -- manual confirmation`, deposit_after = `deposit date > unjournal pub date`, research_area = main_cause_cat_abbrev, nb_link = notebookLM_link, pub_status = publication_status, wp_date = working_paper_release_date, uj_pub_date = publication_date_unjournal ) # Define ordered factor for adjustment status adj_levels <- c( "evidence of updating", "Stated intention to update", "mixed evidence/minor updating", "Unlikely to update", "" ) adj_labels <- c( "Evidence of updating", "Stated intention to update", "Mixed / minor updating", "Unlikely to update", "Not yet assessed" ) df <- df |> mutate( adj_status_clean = case_when( adj_status == "evidence of updating" ~ "Evidence of updating", adj_status == "Stated intention to update" ~ "Stated intention to update", adj_status == "mixed evidence/minor updating" ~ "Mixed / minor updating", adj_status == "Unlikely to update" ~ "Unlikely to update", TRUE ~ "Not yet assessed" ), adj_status_clean = factor(adj_status_clean, levels = adj_labels), author_response_clean = case_when( author_response == "Formal response" ~ "Formal response", author_response == "Informal" ~ "Informal response", author_response == "None?" ~ "No response", TRUE ~ "Not yet coded" ) ) # Color palette aligned with project theme adj_colors <- c( "Evidence of updating" = "#2D9D5E", "Stated intention to update" = "#5AE08A", "Mixed / minor updating" = "#E8722A", "Unlikely to update" = "#C45A1E", "Not yet assessed" = "#CBD5E1" ) theme_uj <- function(base_size = 12) { theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) + theme( panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), axis.text = element_text(size = base_size * 0.85), plot.caption = element_text(size = base_size * 0.75, color = "grey50"), legend.position = "right" ) } ``` ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-summary="Compute headline statistics"} n_total <- nrow(df) n_assessed <- df |> filter(adj_status_clean != "Not yet assessed") |> nrow() n_evidence <- df |> filter(adj_status_clean == "Evidence of updating") |> nrow() n_intention <- df |> filter(adj_status_clean == "Stated intention to update") |> nrow() n_any_positive <- df |> filter(adj_status_clean %in% c("Evidence of updating", "Stated intention to update", "Mixed / minor updating")) |> nrow() n_formal <- df |> filter(author_response_clean == "Formal response") |> nrow() n_any_response <- df |> filter(author_response_clean %in% c("Formal response", "Informal response")) |> nrow() ``` ::: Of **57 tracked evaluations**: - **19** papers received a formal or informal author response - **16** papers received a **formal written response** to the evaluation - **5** papers show **clear evidence of substantive updating** in response to the evaluation - **7** authors stated intention to update their paper - **15** papers show at least some positive signal (updating, intention, or minor revisions) - **22** of 57 have been manually assessed; the remainder are too recent or pending follow-up ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} df |> count(adj_status_clean) |> ggplot(aes(x = reorder(adj_status_clean, -n), y = n, fill = adj_status_clean)) + geom_col(width = 0.65, show.legend = FALSE) + geom_text(aes(label = n), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.5) + scale_fill_manual(values = adj_colors) + scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) + labs(x = NULL, y = "Number of papers", title = "Author adjustment outcomes following Unjournal evaluations") + theme_uj() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 15, hjust = 1)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Distribution of adjustment outcomes across tracked Unjournal evaluations. 'Not yet assessed' includes papers that are too recent or where follow-up is pending.](paper_response_analysis_files/figure-html/fig-adj-bar-1.png){#fig-adj-bar width=672} ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} resp_colors <- c( "Formal response" = "#2B7CE9", "Informal response" = "#5DA3F5", "No response" = "#CBD5E1", "Not yet coded" = "#E2E8F0" ) df |> count(author_response_clean) |> ggplot(aes(x = reorder(author_response_clean, -n), y = n, fill = author_response_clean)) + geom_col(width = 0.55, show.legend = FALSE) + geom_text(aes(label = n), vjust = -0.4, size = 3.5) + scale_fill_manual(values = resp_colors) + scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) + labs(x = NULL, y = "Number of papers", title = "Type of author response to evaluation") + theme_uj() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 15, hjust = 1)) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Type of author response to Unjournal evaluation.](paper_response_analysis_files/figure-html/fig-response-bar-1.png){#fig-response-bar width=672} ::: ::: ## Full Tabulation The table below covers all 57 tracked evaluations. Click column headers to sort; use the search box to filter. Adjustment status is color-coded: green = positive signal, orange = minor/uncertain, grey = unlikely or not yet assessed. ::: {#tbl-full .cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-summary="Build interactive DT table"} # Build display table tbl <- df |> mutate( # Linked paper title title_linked = if_else( !is.na(pubpub_link) & pubpub_link != "", paste0('', str_trunc(paper_title, 70), ''), str_trunc(paper_title, 70) ), # Shorten authors authors_short = str_trunc(authors, 45), # NotebookLM icon link nb_icon = if_else( !is.na(nb_link) & nb_link != "", paste0('📖'), "" ), # DOI link doi_linked = if_else( !is.na(doi) & doi != "" & !str_detect(doi, "^doi\\.org"), paste0('DOI'), if_else( !is.na(doi) & doi != "", paste0('DOI'), "" ) ) ) |> select( Paper = title_linked, Authors = authors_short, Area = research_area, Response = author_response_clean, Adjustment = adj_status_clean, `Pub. status` = pub_status, NB = nb_icon ) # Color rows by adjustment status adj_bg <- c( "Evidence of updating" = "#d4edda", "Stated intention to update" = "#e8f5e9", "Mixed / minor updating" = "#fff3e0", "Unlikely to update" = "#fce4d4", "Not yet assessed" = "#f8fafc" ) datatable( tbl, escape = FALSE, rownames = FALSE, filter = "top", options = list( pageLength = 15, autoWidth = FALSE, columnDefs = list( list(width = "35%", targets = 0), list(width = "20%", targets = 1), list(width = "10%", targets = 2), list(width = "10%", targets = 3), list(width = "12%", targets = 4), list(width = "10%", targets = 5), list(width = "3%", targets = 6) ), dom = "lfrtip" ), caption = "All tracked Unjournal evaluations with author response and adjustment data. NB = link to NotebookLM analysis." ) |> formatStyle( "Adjustment", backgroundColor = styleEqual( names(adj_bg), unname(adj_bg) ) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Selected Public Statements Authors whose responses appear below have made public statements (published on The Unjournal's PubPub platform) about the evaluation process or their plans for revisions. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code code-summary="Display public author quotes"} quotes <- df |> filter(!is.na(pub_statement) & str_trim(pub_statement) != "") |> mutate( short_title = str_trunc(paper_title, 80), pubpub_url = if_else(!is.na(pubpub_link) & pubpub_link != "", pubpub_link, NA_character_) ) |> arrange(adj_status_clean) if (nrow(quotes) == 0) { cat("No public statements recorded yet.\n") } else { for (i in seq_len(nrow(quotes))) { r <- quotes[i, ] title_str <- if (!is.na(r$pubpub_url)) { paste0("[", r$short_title, "](", r$pubpub_url, ")") } else { r$short_title } cat(paste0( "> ", str_trim(r$pub_statement), "\n\n", "> — *", title_str, "*", " (", r$adj_status_clean, ")\n\n" )) } } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` > I’m not very calibrated on this given my limited exposure to academia. But I’d put it in terms of 85th percentile of feedback I’ve received on my work. > — *[The wellbeing cost-effectiveness of StrongMinds and Friendship Bench: Combini...](https://unjournal.pubpub.org/pub/evalsumstrongminds/)* (Stated intention to update) > "We are very grateful to Romain Espinosa and Joshua Tasoff for their thorough reading of our paper and their constructive comments, which will be helpful in preparing a revised version” > — *[Willful Ignorance and Moral Behavior](https://unjournal.pubpub.org/pub/evalsummoralbhvr/)* (Stated intention to update) > [See their ‘authors response’, with feedback on The Unjournal’s approaches] We thank the Unjournal for identifying our paper as highly relevant to inform global priorities, and for Eduardo Masset and Rachel Sabates-Wheeler for taking the time to read and provide comments as part of the review process. > — *[Social Safety Nets, Women’s Economic Achievements and Agency](https://unjournal.pubpub.org/pub/evalsumsafetynets/draft?access=f88pmj31)* (Mixed / minor updating) > The length and thoroughness of their evaluations clearly demonstrate the significant time and intellectual effort they invested in engaging deeply with our research. We are truly grateful for their insightful and constructive comments, which reflect a genuine commitment to advancing the quality and impact of research in this important field. We also express our sincere appreciation to the editors of The Unjournal… Their support made this valuable dialogue possible and highlighted new perspectives on our work. Since our paper has already been published in Management Science, we do not intend to provide a detailed point-by-point response at this stage. Nevertheless, we find the evaluators’ suggestions and reflections very valuable and will carefully consider them as we continue our research agenda and develop future projects. We welcome this opportunity for public scientific discourse and hope that these evaluations encourage further inquiry and application in the realm of online charitable fundraising. > — *[Does online fundraising increase charitable giving? A nationwide field experi...](https://unjournal.pubpub.org/pub/evalsumfundraisingcharitablegiving/)* (Unlikely to update) > [Positive, shows they read it, but fairly generic] We appreciate the reviewers and evaluation managers' comments. While we strove to sufficiently isolate the plausibly exogenous spatiotemporal variation in the irrigation intervention to allow for reliable causal identification, we understand that some readers may still have concerns. We agree with the evaluation managers' suggestion that future work could gather more details on the precise process of treatment assignment (recognizing that we did spend considerable effort toward this already). We also concur with the reviewers comments that further exploring all of the mechanisms behind our diverse results could also help readers in generalizing findings to other contexts. > — *[Irrigation Strengthens Climate Resilience: Long-term Evidence from Mali using...](https://unjournal.pubpub.org/pub/evalsumirrigationresilience/)* (Unlikely to update) ``` ::: ::: ## Automated Change Detection (Supplement) The [paper change analysis tool](https://daaronr.github.io/unjournal_tools_interfaces/paper_change_analysis/) provides automated, reproducible detection of line-level changes between pre- and post-evaluation PDF versions. It: 1. Extracts text from "before" (evaluated) and "after" (latest available) PDF versions 2. Computes line-level additions, deletions, and net text change 3. Optionally uses an LLM to attribute specific changes to evaluator suggestions This supplements the manual coding above by providing objective, quantitative change metrics — particularly useful for papers where subjective judgment of "updating" is difficult. ::: {.callout-note collapse="true"} ## Running the automated pipeline Results from the automated pipeline will appear here once re-run on current paper pairs. To reproduce: ```bash # Install dependencies pip install pandas pdfplumber rapidfuzz # Run from the paper_change_analysis directory of unjournal_tools_interfaces python scripts/analyze_paper_changes.py # Optional: LLM attribution (requires OpenAI key) python scripts/llm_change_attribution.py ``` See full documentation at [https://daaronr.github.io/unjournal_tools_interfaces/paper_change_analysis/](https://daaronr.github.io/unjournal_tools_interfaces/paper_change_analysis/). ::: From an earlier run on 34 paper pairs (a subset of the above), the automated analysis found: - 20 papers had matched Unjournal evaluations (title-based matching from evaluation markdown files) - 6 papers showed both a matched evaluation and substantial line-level revisions (>50 line changes) - 1 paper had over 3,000 net line changes post-evaluation These automated results are consistent with the manual coding above. The discrepancy in totals (34 vs 57) reflects that the manual tracking has since been extended to more papers.
